knowledge_point.title: Finding a Scalar Factor When Direction Reverses

question.:question/problem:
The three vectors share an origin, and each grid square has the same side length.

![](822ab650b6a2146060b82d748248.png)

Given $\mathbf{c}=\lambda\mathbf{a}+3\mathbf{b}$, find $\lambda$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
First trace $3\mathbf{b}$ from the common origin $O$ to a point $P$: keep its direction and scale its length. The remaining path from $P$ to the endpoint $C$ must be the unknown multiple of $\mathbf{a}$.

![](a7138914cf5adc5c2db2ea9724b7.png)

Following the grid direction of $\mathbf{a}$ takes $2$ steps, while the parallel path $PC$ has $4$ steps. Their length ratio is $\frac{4}{2}=2$. The remaining path points in the opposite direction to $\mathbf{a}$, so
$$
\overrightarrow{PC}=-2\mathbf{a}.
$$
Adding the path vectors gives
$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbf{c}&=\overrightarrow{OP}+\overrightarrow{PC}\\
&=3\mathbf{b}+(-2\mathbf{a})\\
&=-2\mathbf{a}+3\mathbf{b}.
\end{aligned}
$$
Because $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ are nonparallel, these coefficients are unique. Comparing with $\mathbf{c}=\lambda\mathbf{a}+3\mathbf{b}$ gives $\lambda=-2$. The minus sign records the reversed direction.

question.:question/worked-solution:

![](0316f6673a47a111da165f4ae265.png)

Following the grid direction of $\mathbf{a}$ takes $4$ steps, while the parallel path $PC$ has $8$ steps. Their length ratio is $\frac{8}{4}=2$. The remaining path points in the opposite direction to $\mathbf{a}$, so
$$
\overrightarrow{PC}=-2\mathbf{a}.
$$
Adding the path vectors gives
$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbf{c}&=\overrightarrow{OP}+\overrightarrow{PC}\\
&=2\mathbf{b}+(-2\mathbf{a})\\

\end{aligned}
$$
Because $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ are nonparallel, these coefficients are unique. Comparing with $\mathbf{c}=\lambda\mathbf{a}+2\mathbf{b}$ gives $\lambda=-2$. The minus sign records the reversed direction.
